title: Read groups and namespaces
summary: A namespace is a path that helps locate a GitLab project. Groups and subgroups can add levels to that path.
introduction: A namespace is a path that helps locate a GitLab project. Groups and subgroups can add levels to that path. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A namespace is a path that helps locate a GitLab project. Groups and subgroups can add levels to that path.

blocks.code:
Example path: school-club/web/reading-list
Top group: school-club
Subgroup: web
Project: reading-list
blocks.title: Read groups and namespaces

blocks.text: The path shows where the project is organised. Two projects in different namespaces can have the same final project name.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Split the fictional path club/mobile/book-checker into its parts.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A path is not proof that a project is official or trustworthy; inspect its owner and content.
For more detail later, use this [GitLab further reading](https://docs.gitlab.com/tutorials/).

seo.title: GitLab: Read groups and namespaces
seo.description: Learn about read groups and namespaces in GitLab. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
